ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there are two squares with aligned bottom sides and adjacent left and right, the left one is smaller, with side length a; the right one is larger, with side length b, and a<b. The three vertices of the gray triangle are respectively the lower-left corner of the left small square, the upper-right corner of the left small square (also on the left boundary of the large square), and the upper-right corner of the right large square. Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, take the lower-left corner of the small square as A=(0,0). Because the side length of the small square is a, and it is aligned with the bottom side of the large square, the upper-right corner of the small square is B=(a,a). The large square starts from x=a, with side length b, so its upper-right corner is C=(a+b,b). The gray triangle is triangle ABC. Using the determinant area formula: Area = 1/2 |det(B-A, C-A)| = 1/2 |det((a,a),(a+b,b))| = 1/2 |a·b - a(a+b)| = 1/2 |-a^2| = 1/2 a^2.

raw_record.question_text: The diagram shows two adjoining squares with side lengths $a$ and $b$ (with $a<b$). How big is the area of the grey triangle?

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and a determinant area formula. From the image, take the bottom-left corner of the smaller square as A=(0,0). Since the left square has side a and is bottom-aligned with the larger square, its top-right corner, which lies on the left side of the larger square, is B=(a,a). Since the right square of side b starts at x=a and has height b, its top-right corner is C=(a+b,b). The grey triangle is triangle ABC, bounded by the diagonal of the small square, the segment from B to the top-right corner of the large square, and the long segment from A to that top-right corner. Compute its area as 1/2 |det(B-A, C-A)| = 1/2 |a b - a(a+b)| = 1/2 a^2.
